The temperature dependence of this early developmental milestone is notable, as the onset of feeding in many marine teleosts is tightly linked to ambient thermal regimes. These foundational life-history parameters provide a critical baseline for understanding the species overall demographic strategy.

This minuscule initial mass, among the smallest recorded for any pentacerotid, reflects an energetically cheap per-offspring investment consistent with a highly fecund, broadcast-spawning reproductive strategy. The yolk-sac larva that emerges is entirely dependent on endogenous reserves during its first few days of exogenous feeding onset, a critical period during which mortality is typically very high in the pelagic environment.

This extended lifespan places the Yellowspotted boarfish among the more durable members of its order, consistent with a life-history strategy that prioritizes slow growth, deferred reproduction, and repeated spawning events over many seasons. The corresponding wet weight at puberty of 2.44 kilograms [Wwp = 2.44 kilograms] and the ultimate wet weight for males of 20.9 kilograms [Wwi = 20.9 kilograms] illustrate a considerable scope for post-maturation growth, with individuals continuing to add mass for many years after reaching sexual maturity.
